titel: Vance Bombs at Brutal Town Hall

einzeiler: Trump shifts on Russia, GOP plans for midterms, and an interview with Mayor Paige…
kurzfassung: The hosts analyze Donald Trump's shifting stance on Russia, the fallout from short-lived White House press secretary Katie Zachariah's departure, and Republican messaging on international events like the protests in France. They also examine the tight Senate race in Michigan, focusing on Abdul El-Sayed's tense town hall exchange. Finally, Scranton Mayor Paige Cognetti joins the show to discuss her congressional campaign and anti-corruption platform.
stichpunkte: Trump signs an executive order rolling back bipartisan sanctions on Russia, sparking criticism over his approach to Vladimir Putin.
The hosts discuss the bizarre web of controversies surrounding Alina Habba, her husband, and Rick Grinnell regarding the Kennedy Center.
Katie Zachariah's historically brief tenure as White House press secretary comes to an end following a disastrous media appearance.
Republicans attempt to use the protests in France as a warning about immigration and Democratic policies ahead of the midterms.
Trump publicly criticizes Fox News for not being sufficiently supportive, urging his followers to watch alternative networks instead.
In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed faces a hostile question from a Republican operative at a town hall, leading to a viral exchange.
The Maine Senate race attracts national attention following a blunt debate exchange between Troy Jackson and Susan Collins.
J.D. Vance's recent town hall appearance in Michigan showcases an awkward attempt to project a more moderate, relatable image.
Scranton Mayor Paige Cognetti joins the show to discuss her anti-corruption campaign and her race for the U.S. House in Pennsylvania.

clips.hook: Did Putin play Trump like a fiddle on an energy ceasefire?
clips.text: The hosts discuss how Vladimir Putin may have manipulated Trump into proposing a one-sided energy ceasefire that exclusively benefited Russian interests.

clips.hook: Fired on live television after just five days on the job.
clips.text: The speakers marvel at the record-breaking brevity of Katie Zachariah's time as press secretary, lasting only five days and a single briefing.

clips.hook: Why political attacks on family ties are designed to mislead.
clips.text: The host breaks down how opponents weaponize obscure foreign associations and family histories to smear candidates who have no personal connection to those groups.

clips.hook: J.D. Vance jokes about the Socialist Republic of Brooklyn.
clips.text: During a town hall, J.D. Vance engages in surprisingly lighthearted banter with an audience member who lives in New York.

clips.hook: Why broken promises on the Epstein files are driving voter regret.
clips.text: Mayor Paige Cognetti explains that voters in her district feel deeply betrayed by unfulfilled promises regarding transparency and accountability for high-profile scandals.

beschreibung:
Vice President JD Vance tries and fails to act normal during a CBS town hall in Michigan — but struggles even harder to explain away his boss's policies. Donald Trump sells out Ukraine to Vladimir Putin, a complex scandal involving two Trump advisors engulfs the White House, new details emerge about the firing of Katie Zacharia, and Republicans try to make an issue out of the riots in France.
Jon, Lovett, and Tommy react to all the latest, including new lines of attack in the Senate races in Michigan and Maine, and Trump telling his followers not watch Fox News anymore. Then, Mayor Paige Cognetti talks to Jon about fighting corruption in Pennsylvania and flipping a critical House seat blue.
